sentences.text: Pooja Joshi vs Akshat Joshi on 9 August, 2024

Author: Sanjay Kumar
Bench: Sanjay Kumar
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No. 2336 Of 2023
 Pooja Joshi ..... Petit
 Versus
 Akshat Joshi ..... Respo
 O R D E R
Parties have entered into a settlement agreement.

Payment of 10,00,000/- (Rupees ten lakhs only)
by way of demand draft has been made by the respondent, Akshat Joshi, to the petitioner, Pooja Joshi.

The other terms and conditions of the settlement concerning the return of Streedhan,
jewellery etc., have also been implemented.
The petitioner, Pooja Joshi, and the respondent, Akshat Joshi, had gotten married on 15.04.2007 at Agra, Uttar Pradesh.
However, they have been living separately since 2019.
Proceedings1 under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 19732, were initiated by the petitioner, Pooja Joshi on 03.10.2019.
She also instituted proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act, 20053 on 09.12.2019.

At her behest, First Information Report4 No. 43/2022 dated 25.05.2022, for offence(s)
punishable under Sections 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Deepak Guglani Date: 2024.08.14 1 MJCR-191/2019 pending before the Principal Judge,
Family Court, Shahdol, Madhya 17:21:59 IST Reason:
Pradesh 2 For short, Cr.P.C..
3 For short, DV Act.
4 For short, FIR.
Prohibition Act, 1961, was registered at Police Station  Shahdol, District Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text:
Principal Judge,
Family Court, Shahdol, Madhya
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent, Akshat Joshi, had filed a petition5 for dissolution of the marriage under Section 13(1A) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which is pending.
Pooja Joshi vs Akshat Joshi on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132802350/
1 In view of the settlement agreement between the parties, which is taken on record, we accept their prayer and dissolve the marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

We also exercise our power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India and quash FIR No.
43/2022 for offence(s) punishable under Sections 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, that was registered at Police Station  Shahdol,
District Shahdol, Madhya Pradesh.
Proceedings under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C. and under the provisions of the DV Act will be treated as disposed of.
The transfer petition is allowed and disposed of in the above terms.

Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
